title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your makerspace assistant for ten minutes, and the assistant keeps track of everything said. What makes this possible?

options.text: The program sends the earlier messages to the model on every call
The model updates itself with each message so that it learns the chat
The model keeps a private store of messages between its calls
The context window is a permanent store that is never emptied

items.stem: The instructions and tool descriptions take 2,000 tokens and the student's question takes 100. Call 1 sends these and the model replies with a 50-token tool request. The tool returns a 400-token result, and call 2 sends everything so far and returns the final answer. Counting only input tokens, how many tokens were sent across the two calls in total?
Your assistant should greet a returning student with the machines they completed training on last month. Which design provides this?

options.text: Choose a model whose context window is large enough to last a month
Keep that student's old conversation open and continue it next visit
Store a record outside the model and load it when the visit starts
Put every student's training list into the shared instructions text

items.stem: A teammate suggests pasting all twelve machine manuals into the assistant's instructions so it never needs to search. Give one reason, in a sentence, this is a poor idea for your assistant.
A long scheduling task has nearly filled the context window, and the agent must continue the same task. Which technique fits best?

options.text: Delete the system instructions so the window has room again
Summarize the work so far, then continue in a fresh window
Restart the task from nothing and discard all progress so far
Send the rest of the task to the model without any context
